adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` an array and, for COLLECTIVE team events, `handleNewBooking` collects additional hosts' destination calendars into `evt.destinationCalendar` (lines ~970-1070) and later pushes them (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). However, when persisting the booking, it only connects `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` to `Booking.destinationCalendar` (handleNewBooking.ts ~1871-1879), meaning only the first destination calendar is stored on the booking record. All downstream code shown reconstructs `evt.destinationCalendar` from the booking relation as a single-element array (e.g., handleCancelBooking.ts ~248-255 / ~508-515, confirm.handler.ts ~172-179, editLocation.handler.ts ~82-89, payments webhook.ts ~98-120, requestReschedule.handler.ts ~237-243), so additional collective hosts' destination calendars are lost after creation. Flows that rely on the reconstructed `evt.destinationCalendar` (rather than stored references) will therefore only target the first host calendar.
